title: WAF Blocked Request Analysis

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.1.19 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.1.19 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:waf` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.

detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws` with the modular input for `aws:waf`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.1.78.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `action` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable WAF logging to S3 or Kinesis Firehose. Ingest via Splunk_TA_aws. Analyze blocked requests by rule, source IP, URI, and user agent to identify attack patterns and false positives.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:waf" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:waf" action="BLOCK"
| table _time action terminatingRuleId httpRequest.clientIp httpRequest.uri
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.19_waf_blocked_request_anal_19"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:waf` in `index=aws` to detect waf blocked request analysis. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the AWS WAF console Sampled requests for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `action` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_1_19_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Table (rule, source, URI, count), Bar chart by rule, Map (source IPs), Timeline..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of waf blocked request analysis so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
